items.title: Gradient-only approximate proximal execution: certificate and pointwise work

source.anchor: Appendix D.2, Algorithm D.2 and Lemma D.3, equations D.5–D.6
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib restatement and expanded derivation; not the authors' original wording or an endorsement.

items.statement: For a C² potential with kappa-inverse and unit Hessian bounds, the iteration x₀=y, xₙ₊₁=y−eta∇V(xₙ) stops at its first residual at most (1−eta)eps. It returns the current iterate, within eps of the unique proximal minimum. Its gradient-query count, including the successful test, is bounded by C_c[1+log(1+‖∇V(y)‖/eps)], uniformly in y, for fixed 0<eta≤c<1. Samplinglib additionally establishes measurable first-hit/output, quantitative unique minimum and the exact finite-fuel execution equation.
assumptions: The source uses Euclidean space; the formal statement uses a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.
V is C², kappa≥1 and kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖² for every x,v.
0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0. Exact arithmetic and exact gradient queries are the cost model, not floating-point arithmetic.

obligations.label: Finite first residual success and measurable stopped output
Genuine proximal identification and epsilon certificate
Actual finite-fuel execution with logarithmic query count

bindings.boundary: Pointwise D.2/D.3 execution only. Expected work along the realized Picard run (D.4), D.1 stability, sampling accuracy and the main paper remain separate. The interpreter records point/count but not a query-list trace; its successful fuel is N+1, with no arbitrary-excess-fuel theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: Finite-dimensional Euclidean potential and curvature bounds.
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space, C² V, genuine Hessian bounds and kappa≥1.
assumption_deltas.reason: Coordinate-free representation includes the source Euclidean setting; C² ensures totalized fderiv denotes the genuine Hessian.
The contraction proof covers the full stated parameter range.

assumption_deltas.source: Return the current tested iterate; count gradient evaluations.
assumption_deltas.reason: Every tested residual spends one query, including the successful test. This does not model floating-point rounding or export machine code.

assumption_deltas.source: C_c₀ depends only on c₀; proximity to the proximal point.
assumption_deltas.lean: An explicit finite C_c and quadratic growth at the unique proximal minimum; measurable p, N and stopped output.
assumption_deltas.reason: These are derived certificates and measurability details, not extra premises. No integration or expected-cost claim is made.
